sections.title: Section B - Data and experimental skills

stem: A transmission electron micrograph shows a chloroplast containing a double envelope, grana, intergranal lamellae, stroma and small ribosome-like particles.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (i) Draw a labelled diagram containing four structures visible in the chloroplast.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (ii) Distinguish the ribosomes in the chloroplast from ribosomes free in the cytoplasm.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (iii) State one organelle that modifies and packages a protein for secretion.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Explain how a student could prepare and observe a temporary leaf epidermis mount to examine stomata.

questions.title: Chloroplasts and microscopy

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (i) [3] Award for a clear double envelope and any three correctly positioned labels: granum/thylakoids, intergranal lamella, stroma, starch grain or ribosome.

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (ii) [2] Chloroplast ribosomes are 70S and smaller; cytoplasmic ribosomes are 80S and larger.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Peel a thin epidermal layer; place flat in water/stain on a clean slide; lower coverslip at an angle to avoid bubbles; begin with low power, focus and then increase magnification.

stem: A student recorded heart rate and stroke volume at four stages of a cycling trial.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (i) Calculate cardiac output during intense exercise in dm3 min-1.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (ii) Compare the changes in heart rate and stroke volume from rest to intense exercise.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (iii) Explain why blood flow to skeletal muscle increases during exercise.

parts.label: b
parts.html: (i) State one structural adaptation of capillaries for rapid exchange.

parts.label: b
parts.html: (ii) Distinguish arteries from veins using two structural features.

questions.title: Cardiovascular response to exercise

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (ii) [2] Both increase. Heart rate rises by 103 bpm (about 151%), whereas stroke volume rises by 36 cm3 (50%); heart rate changes proportionally more.

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (iii) [2] Active muscle has greater oxygen/glucose demand and produces more carbon dioxide/heat; arterioles dilate to increase delivery and removal.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: (i) [1] Wall is one endothelial cell thick; narrow lumen; extensive network/large total surface area; pores in some tissues.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: (ii) [2] Arteries have thicker muscular/elastic walls and smaller lumen; veins have thinner walls, larger lumen and valves.

stem: Root tips were placed horizontally in darkness. In group A, the root cap remained intact. In group B, the cap was removed. In group C, the cap was covered by an impermeable cap. After 18 hours, only group A curved downward.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (i) Identify the response shown by group A.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (ii) Suggest a suitable control for testing whether the impermeable cap itself prevents growth.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (iii) Explain why group A curves but groups B and C do not.

parts.label: b
parts.html: (i) Agar blocks were placed under intact root caps for 0, 2, 4 and 6 hours, then transferred to decapped roots. Predict the trend in curvature.

questions.title: Plant growth responses

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (ii) [1] Use an intact root with an identical cap that is permeable, or place the impermeable cap away from the tip.

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (iii) [3] The cap detects gravity; auxin is redistributed to the lower side; in roots, higher auxin inhibits elongation so the upper side grows faster; removing or isolating the cap prevents detection/signal transfer.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: (i) [2] Longer contact allows more growth-regulating substance to diffuse into agar, so curvature/growth response increases to a maximum as exposure time increases.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: (ii) [1] Angle of curvature, change in root-tip position, or difference in side lengths after a fixed time.

stem: Students counted 170 cells in a root meristem. The results are shown in the table.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (ii) Suggest why more cells are seen in prophase than anaphase.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Distinguish the products of mitosis and meiosis.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain how meiosis and outcrossing in a hermaphroditic flowering plant can increase variation among offspring.

questions.title: Cell division and genetic variation

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (ii) [1] Cells spend longer in prophase, so a random snapshot includes more prophase cells.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Mitosis produces two genetically near-identical cells with unchanged chromosome number; meiosis produces four genetically different haploid cells with halved chromosome number.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Crossing over in prophase I; independent assortment/segregation; random fertilization; pollen from another individual combines alleles from different parents; self-incompatibility/different maturation times can promote outcrossing.

instructions: Answer every structured question. Show working, use units and significant figures appropriately, and support conclusions with evidence from the supplied data.
